Review of Enacted State Budget Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance The Finance and Facilities Committee reviewed the FY27 state budget approved by the General Assembly on June 9, 2026.
Vice President Abby Benson reported that the General Assembly approved a $4.2 million increase to the operating budget, an amount in line with the Governor’s Recommended Budget (GRB), but well below the University’s request of $37.6 million.
She reminded the Committee of the three categories for the request: Operating Budget Shortfall, Current Service Level, and Strategic Initiatives, of which only the Current Service Level was funded.
She noted that of the $4.2 million increase in the operating budget, $1.3 million of this amount reflects support for corresponding expenses imposed by the state for centralized services.
Strategic Initiatives have not been funded for a number of years, but the University continues to maintain this request to signal the importance of these initiatives.

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 14, 2026 SUBJECT: Discussion: Update on URI Workday Implementation Purpose of Submittal: Update the Board of Trustees on the implementation of Workday at the University of Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: The University of Rhode Island launched its Workday implementation on January 12, 2026, to replace its PeopleSoft Human Resources and Finance systems and the PBCS budgeting platform.
The project has successfully completed the Planning stage and is currently in the Architect and Configure stage, where functional and technical teams are configuring business requirements, validating system design, and testing configurations to ensure alignment with institutional needs.
Overall, the implementation remains on track across the majority of workstreams and continues to perform within planned timeline and budget expectations.

Project leadership and governance have remained stable and effective, providing consistent oversight and decision-making throughout the implementation.
State system integration remains the most significant project risk.
Identified early in the implementation, this dependency continues to present challenges because critical aspects of the integration effort are outside the direct control of URI and rely on State of Rhode Island stakeholders and timelines.
URI and the State of Rhode Island leadership team have been meeting monthly on the project status.
Change management continues to be a key factor for the implementation.
Over the past several weeks, outreach and engagement efforts have increased to provide opportunities for faculty, staff, and campus stakeholders to learn about the Workday program.
These activities are focused on building awareness, preparing the University community for upcoming changes, and driving adoption to support a successful transition to the new system .
Overall, the project remains on track , however we are mindful and maintain focus on risk management, stakeholder engagement, and organizational readiness.

Points to Consider: URI’s external auditors, CliftonLarsonAllen LLP, have completed their audit and have no audit findings.
The University will have a clean audit opinion for the year ending June 30, 2026.
Upon approval by the URI Board of Trustees, the FY 2026 financial statements will be issued.
Please refer to pp. 4-14 of the enclosed draft financial statements for the University’s Management's Discussion and Analysis, which provides a summary of our FY2026 statements.
A few highlights are outlined below. • The University reported an increase in net position of $88.48 million in FY26, up from $65.90 million in FY25.

This includes a $8.18 million decrease in net position before $96.66 million in capital contributions, which significantly contributed to the overall increase. • In FY26, operating revenues increased by $15.92 million (2.96%), compared to a $4.62 million (0.85%) decrease in FY25.
This decrease in FY25 was primarily due to a change in NACUBO reporting guidance that increased the scholarship allowance, which nets against tuition and fees. • Net tuition and fee revenue increased by $16.33 million due to an increase in tuition rates of 3.5% for both in-state students and out -of-state students and an increase in demand for housing, along with stronger retention rates.
Other operating revenues decreased slightly as the University outsourced the bookstore operations. • In FY26, operating expenses for the University increased by $21.93 million (3.2%), compared to a $25.30 million (3.8%) increase FY25.

The increase is comprised primarily of increases in salary and benefits, as well as other operating expenses such as utilities, repairs, and maintenance which have been impacted by broader economic factors. • When reviewing the University’s condensed statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net position, it is important to note that nonoperating revenue plays an important role in supporting the operations of the University.
The primary component of nonoperating revenues is State appropriations.
The State’s unrestricted appropriation represents the largest component of the University’s nonoperating revenues.
